beats.instructions: Press Run. The line print("ember") is already written, and the wall will show that word.

scene.caption: Rain ticks on the road. The gate of Emberkeep is shut, and the wall is ready to show a word.

images.alt: A wet road leading to the shut gate of Emberkeep

activity.failFeedback: Press Run so the word ember shows in the console.

checks.name: the console shows ember
checks.code: assert "ember" in _captured_stdout, "The console should include the word ember."

beats.instructions: Type this line and press Run: print("The gate is shut.")

scene.caption: Iron bars fill the arch. The wall is waiting for a sentence from you.

images.alt: The iron-bound arch of the Emberkeep gate

activity.failFeedback: Type print("The gate is shut.") and press Run.

checks.name: the console shows the sentence
checks.code: assert _captured_stdout.strip() == "The gate is shut.", "The console should show The gate is shut."

beats.instructions: Type a different print and press Run: print("A keeper waits.")

scene.caption: A hooded gatekeeper stands behind the bars and waits.

images.alt: The gatekeeper waiting behind the gate

activity.passFeedback: The wall shows your new sentence.
activity.failFeedback: Type print("A keeper waits.") and press Run.

checks.name: the console shows the new sentence
checks.code: assert _captured_stdout.strip() == "A keeper waits.", "The console should show A keeper waits."

beats.instructions: Type these two lines and press Run: print("The left torch is dark.") and print("The right torch is dark."). The console should show two lines.

scene.caption: Two torches stand in the dark, one on each side of the courtyard.

images.alt: Two dark torches in the Emberkeep courtyard

activity.passFeedback: The wall shows both torch lines.
activity.failFeedback: Type both print lines so the console shows two lines.

checks.name: the console shows two lines
checks.code:
lines = [line.strip() for line in _captured_stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
assert lines == ["The left torch is dark.", "The right torch is dark."], "The console should show the two torch lines."

beats.instructions: The gatekeeper says the wall can remember a word. Press Continue.

scene.caption: The gatekeeper says the wall can remember a word.

images.alt: The gatekeeper speaking at the gate

beats.instructions: A variable remembers a value. Type this line and press Run: word = "ember"

scene.caption: The stones of the arch can hold one word.

images.alt: The stone arch that can remember a word

beats.instructions: Change that same variable to a new word. Type word = "keep" and press Run.

images.alt: The stone arch after the remembered word changes

activity.failFeedback: Change word to "keep" and press Run.

beats.instructions: Remembering a word is not the same as speaking it. Press Continue.

scene.caption: The gatekeeper says remembering a word is not the same as speaking it.

images.alt: The gatekeeper explaining remembering and speaking

beats.instructions: name holds Rowan. print(name) shows the value. print("name") shows the word name. Add print(name) and press Run.

scene.caption: The gatekeeper asks you to speak the name the wall is holding.

images.alt: The gatekeeper asking you to speak a name

activity.failFeedback: Quotes around name make Python show the word name instead of the value, so use print(name).

checks.name: the console shows the value
checks.code:
shown = _captured_stdout.strip()
assert shown == str(name), "The console should show the value of name, not the word name."
assert shown != "name"

beats.instructions: Make a different variable and print it. Type place = "Emberkeep" and then print(place), and press Run.

scene.caption: The road behind you leads to one place.

images.alt: The road that leads to Emberkeep

activity.starterCode: # Remember a place and say it.
activity.failFeedback: Set place to "Emberkeep" and print it with print(place).

checks.name: the console shows the place
checks.code:
shown = _captured_stdout.strip()
assert place == "Emberkeep", "place should remember Emberkeep."
assert shown == "Emberkeep", "The console should show Emberkeep."

beats.instructions: Two torches are dark. The gatekeeper asks what you get if you count both. Press Continue.

scene.caption: Two torches are dark. The gatekeeper asks what you get if you count both.

images.alt: Two dark torches waiting to be counted

beats.instructions: The left torch is 2 and the right torch is 3. Type left = 2 and right = 3, then press Run. Do not print yet.

scene.caption: The left torch counts as 2. The right torch counts as 3.

images.alt: The left and right torches in the dark courtyard

activity.failFeedback: Type left = 2 and right = 3, then press Run.

checks.name: both torch counts are remembered
checks.code:
assert left == 2, "left should be 2."
assert right == 3, "right should be 3."

beats.instructions: Print each number on its own line. Keep left = 2 and right = 3, then type print(left) and print(right), and press Run.

scene.caption: Each torch count can be spoken on its own line.

images.alt: The courtyard torches ready to be spoken

activity.failFeedback: Use print(left) and print(right) so each number is on its own line.

checks.name: each count is on its own line
checks.code:
lines = [line.strip() for line in _captured_stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
assert lines == [str(left), str(right)], "Print each number on its own line."

beats.instructions: Print the sum with print(left + right). Keep left = 2 and right = 3. Adding the numbers gives one total, which is not the same as sticking the two numbers together as text.

scene.caption: The gatekeeper waits for one number: both torches counted together.

images.alt: The courtyard while the two torches are counted together

activity.passFeedback: The console shows 5, the sum of the two torches.
activity.failFeedback: Use print(left + right) so the console shows the sum, not the two numbers stuck together.

checks.name: the console shows the sum
checks.code:
shown = _captured_stdout.strip()
assert left == 2, "left should be 2."
assert right == 3, "right should be 3."
assert shown == str(left + right), "Print the sum of the two numbers."
assert shown != str(left) + str(right), "Print the sum, not the two numbers stuck together."

beats.instructions: Put it together. The gate asks for 4 and 1. Type left = 4, then right = 1, then print(left + right), and press Run.

scene.caption: The gate will answer if you count 4 and 1 and say the sum.

images.alt: The gate arch waiting to answer

activity.starterCode: # Count two numbers and say their sum.
activity.passFeedback: The gate answers 5, the bars rise, and Emberkeep lets you through.
activity.failFeedback: Set left to 4 and right to 1, then print the sum with print(left + right).

checks.name: the console shows the new sum
checks.code:
shown = _captured_stdout.strip()
assert left == 4, "left should be 4."
assert right == 1, "right should be 1."
assert shown == str(left + right), "The console should show the sum of the two numbers."
assert shown != str(left) + str(right), "Print the sum, not the two numbers stuck together."
